methodological_questions: Can play-type labels be built from pre-outcome information without leaking possession results or foul endings?
Is opponent next-possession PPP after play X large enough, relative to a pre-specified threshold, to drive AVOID labels, with confidence intervals and matched baselines?
Do own-sequence lagged outcomes add information beyond the current play type?
What per-cell sample sizes are needed for stable PPP differences by play type and lag?
How should multiplicity across play types and lags be controlled?

historical_evidence.finding: Sequence-level PPP by inferred play type showed SPOT_UP at 2.83 PPP (100% makes) and TRANSITION at 0.62 PPP because the assisted flag exists only on makes. After rewriting play_type_inferrer.py, SPOT_UP was about 1.16 and TRANSITION about 1.20. The record calls this an engineering discovery that poisoned a simulation.

OTHER possessions ended in fouls 36% of the time, which inflated PPP (FOUL_BUCKET). DRIVE sat 12pp below the foul benchmark (FOUL_LEAK). PNR showed a 22% foul rate. Only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) mapped to a real play type via initiation_type.

Label accuracy audit recorded overall FAIL. OTHER was 20.2% against a <10% target, 40.8% of labels were low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw was 1.7% against a 14-22% benchmark, most play types had PPP above the benchmark band, and MIA identity checks failed. Foul possessions leak into OTHER. Recorded verdict: tool_eval_fail.

Extended possession value: 4 of 8 play types showed real downstream opponent next-PPP effects (CUT +0.0220 suppression, TRANSITION +0.0145, SPOT_UP +0.0124, POST_UP +0.0194). DRIVE downstream was not real (opponent ATT +0.0024). Downstream effects were about 0.01 to 0.02 PPP. Player-level downstream results were mostly non-finding after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (BH).

Play-type PPP across playoff series game buckets (EARLY G1-2, MID G3-4, LATE G5-7; 1197 records, no CIs). DRIVE rose +0.060 across the series, so the pre-stated decline hypothesis was not supported. Recorded as NO CLEAR SIGNAL, observational, with selection caveats.

Superstar sequential suppression: PUTBACK was the top opponent-preceding suppressor for 6+ stars (e.g., D. Mitchell 1.178 to 0.884, d=-0.294, n_after=95; B. Beal d=-0.345, n=32; C. Holmgren d=-0.222, n=52). Other top suppressors were TRANSITION and POST_UP with small effects. No multiplicity correction was applied. Several PUTBACK cells had n_after of 32 to 95, against thousands of baseline possessions.

Holdout play-type mix alignment: strength-controlled gap of +3.27 ORtg (+0.0193 vs -0.0134 PPP residual) across 908 holdout game-team rows (454 games). No CI stated. Validation was same-pipeline only. This concerns team mix, not opponent next-possession PPP.

Consolidated record covering sequential pair premium and defensive aftershock. Reports 8 of 8 play types with a positive aftershock replicated across all-games and playoffs (for example CUT +0.119 n=21,398; TRANSITION +0.135 n=26,262), with top pair premiums such as PUTBACK to TRANSITION +0.084 n=565. Aftershock values are about +0.12 to +0.13 for the listed play types. The record is truncated and combines APPA-049 and APPS-037 material; I did not read the full text.

On-ball defensive scheme labels (DROP/ICE/SWITCH). Only 14.9% of DET possessions (10 of 67) and 3.3% of ORL possessions (2 of 60) were labelled. switches_on was unpopulated in the NBA matchups feed. Recorded verdict: failed_gate.

failed_approaches.why: Foul endings contaminated PPP (OTHER 36% foul endings), DRIVE foul rates were 12pp below benchmark, and initiation_type mapped only 0.7% of 50,668 possessions to a real play type.

Label coverage was too sparse (14.9% and 3.3%) and the switches_on field was not populated, so the gate failed.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type PPP decline across playoff series as a basis for DRIVE as an early-series call
failed_approaches.why: No clear signal: DRIVE rose +0.060. The record is observational, with selection caveats and no CIs.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Superstar sequential suppression from specific opponent play types
failed_approaches.why: No multiplicity correction, n_after of 32 to 95 in several PUTBACK cells, and drift/non-stationarity risk.

evidence_establishes: Play-type labels built from the current play-by-play have failed multiple audits: leakage from outcome fields (assisted flag), foul-ending contamination, and very low coverage of initiation_type. Any AVOID rule built on these labels inherits that error (FAM:SF-PAP-096, FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF-APPM-014).

Downstream opponent next-PPP effects after some play types are small, about 0.01 to 0.02 PPP in the recorded extended-possession analysis. Only 4 of 8 play types showed a real effect and DRIVE did not (FAM:SF-APPS-075).

Sequential and aftershock effects of about +0.12 to +0.13 are reported as replicated for the listed play types, but these concern the offensive next-play value or a defensive aftershock after success and are not the same quantity as opponent next-PPP after play X (FAM:SF07).
Sparse per-cell samples (n of 30 to 95 for some suppressor cells) make single-star or single-cell suppression estimates unstable (FAM:SF-APPA-050).
Player-level downstream findings were mostly non-findings after BH correction (FAM:SF-APPS-075).
evidence_does_not_establish: The records do not define the AVOID rule, the threshold for 'large enough', or how AVOID labels would be used, so the question as posed cannot be tested against a specified decision.

No returned record estimates opponent next-possession PPP after play X with confidence intervals, a matched baseline, and clean labels. The closest records (APPS-075, SF07) use different constructions or report no CIs.
No record establishes that own-sequence lagged outcomes add information beyond the current play type.
Whether the 2025-26 season or playoff data, or the 2022-23 to 2024-25 data, behaves stably over time is not addressed by any record except the drift flag in APPA-050.
The SF07 record is truncated and its status is recorded as supported, but the full text was not read, so the replication claim could not be checked here.
own_inferences: The question's causal direction is underspecified: opponent PPP after X could reflect the lineup, the defensive scheme, or the foul-ending leakage already documented, not the play type itself.

The downstream effects recorded in APPS-075 (about 0.01 to 0.02 PPP) are an order of magnitude smaller than the direct PPP gaps the team and labels are built around. A rule that requires a large opponent PPP effect may therefore rarely trigger, or trigger on noise.

Rough power estimate (my own calculation, not from a record): with possession-level PPP SD of about 1.2, detecting a 0.02 PPP difference at 80% power and alpha 0.05 needs roughly 55,000 possessions per group. Many play-type by lag cells would fall far short of that.
The 2025-26 playoffs were partial on 2026-06-19 and the 2025-26 regular season was complete only from 2026-04-13, so the usable sample for this date is restricted to complete games.
uncertainties: The AVOID label definition, threshold, and downstream decision use are not in the task or the records.
Current label quality after the play_type_inferrer rewrite is unknown; no record re-audits the rebuilt labels.
Whether foul-ending possessions were removed or re-coded in the rebuilt labels is not stated.
The overlap between the APP slices and the SF07 aftershock sample (noted as possible overlap in PAP-096) could inflate apparent replication.
Several records have auto_validation_status of no_validation_recorded, so their reported effects have not been independently validated.
Opponent strength, lineup, and game-state confounders are not controlled in any retrieved analysis that reports opponent PPP.

historical_effect.explanation: Historical records showed that the play-type labels that would feed AVOID rules have failed audits for outcome leakage and foul contamination, and that the downstream opponent PPP effects that the question depends on are small and inconsistent across play types. Together these moved the decision from a plain test to do_not_proceed as posed. A minimum viable test with rebuilt labels, a pre-set threshold, and CIs is specified below as the path forward.

blocking_constraints.text: Play-type labels have been derived from outcome fields (assisted flag, makes only) and foul endings, so PPP by label is partly an outcome measure (FAM:SF-PAP-096, FAM:SF-CHT-025).
The label audit failed on OTHER share, foul-draw benchmarks, and team identity checks (FAM:SF-APPM-014).
Expected downstream effects of about 0.01 to 0.02 PPP need on the order of tens of thousands of possessions per cell; some suppressor cells had n of 30 to 95 (FAM:SF-APPS-075, FAM:SF-APPA-050).
Multiple play types, lags, and player cuts were tested without correction in APPA-050, and the question adds further lag comparisons.

prior_work.summary: Earlier work partly addresses the question. Opponent next-PPP effects after play types were estimated in APPS-075 (about 0.01 to 0.02 PPP for 4 of 8 play types) and in APPA-050 (sequential suppression, mostly underpowered and uncorrected). SF07 reports aftershock/pair effects as supported, but its construction differs from the question. Label-validity audits (PAP-096, CHT-025, APPM-014) show the labels that an AVOID rule needs have not been validated. The specific AVOID-threshold question is not answered by any retrieved record.

risks.text: Labels that use the assisted flag or foul outcomes make PPP by label circular.
Audit failures on OTHER share (20.2%), foul-draw rate (1.7%), and identity checks.
Any label that uses the possession's own outcome or later events to define the sequence leaks future information into the opponent next-PPP measure.
initiation_type maps only 0.7% of possessions to a real play type; the derived possession records may not be reproducible at scale.
Downstream effects of 0.01 to 0.02 PPP require very large cell counts; several cells had n of 30 to 95.
Opponent quality, lineup, game state, and fouls can drive next-possession PPP independently of play type X.
Play types, lags, and players are tested together; APPA-050 applied no correction.
Four seasons of data, with 2025-26 partial, may shift rates; APPA-050 flagged drift.
Without a placebo lag or shuffled-label check, apparent suppression could reflect the selection of cells rather than a true effect.

design.estimand: For each play type X and lag L in {-1, +1}, the difference in opponent next-possession PPP after X versus a matched baseline of opponent possessions, with 95% CIs. The AVOID rule is triggered only if the suppression exceeds a threshold fixed before analysis (for example, the lower 95% bound must exceed a pre-registered PPP delta). Own-sequence lag effects are estimated separately with the same structure.
design.unit: Possession: the opponent's possession immediately after a team possession labelled X (lag +1), and the team's own next possession (lag +1 own-sequence).
design.sample: Complete games only: 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season only from games on or after 2026-04-13. Exclude the 2025-26 playoffs, which are partial as of 2026-06-19. Use a frozen data snapshot. Exclude foul-ending and other non-scoring-event possessions from the label, or define them as a separate outcome bucket.
design.power: Before running the test, compute required n per cell for a pre-specified minimum effect (for example 0.02 PPP) at 80% power, alpha 0.05 with Holm correction. My rough estimate is about 55,000 possessions per group. Cells below the required n are reported as underpowered and are not used for AVOID decisions.
design.controls: Use labels built only from pre-outcome information (no assisted flag, no foul or scoring outcome of the labelled possession). Control for opponent offensive and defensive strength, lineup and rotation intervals, score margin, period, clock, and game-state. Use matched baselines by these covariates. Exclude possessions with undefined initiator or with initiation_type mapping failures.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo lag: the opponent play at lag -1 (before X) should show no suppression. (2) Within-game label permutation: shuffled labels should yield no effect. (3) Re-run the audits from FAM:SF-APPM-014 and FAM:SF-CHT-025 on the rebuilt labels; if OTHER share is above 10% or foul-draw falls outside the 14-22% benchmark, the test is halted. (4) Check the SF07 overlap with any APP slice before combining results.
design.multiplicity: Holm correction across play types and lag cells within each lag family; Benjamini-Hochberg reported for player-level cuts. Pre-register the set of play types and lags before analysis; no post hoc cells.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the lower 95% CI bound for opponent next-PPP suppression after X exceeds the pre-registered threshold, passes the placebo-lag and permutation checks, and the labels pass the rebuilt audits. Otherwise report as uncertain or artifact, not as an AVOID trigger. The AVOID threshold itself must be defined before any analysis is run.
design.data_version: Frozen per-game snapshot of the NBA stats API files (play-by-play, rotations, starters, matchup minutes, box score) and the derived Neo4j possession records, dated with the snapshot. Includes 2022-23 to 2024-25 complete seasons and playoffs, and the 2025-26 regular season from games on or after 2026-04-13. Excludes the 2025-26 playoffs as partial on 2026-06-19.

methodological_questions: Can opponent next-possession PPP after play X be estimated reliably enough to drive AVOID labels?
Do own-sequence lagged outcomes add information beyond the current play type?
How do derived play-type labels built from outcome data create leakage or circularity?
What sample sizes and exposure counts are needed for stable PPP estimates by play type?
